description: We are a team of students interested in space, science, technology, and innovation. We enjoy learning new things, sharing ideas, and solving problems. We are looking for creative and motivated members with skills in coding, design, research, and teamwork who are willing to learn and contribute.
summary:
AstroCare is a web-based astronaut health monitoring dashboard designed to demonstrate how astronaut health information can be presented in a simple and accessible way during space missions. The website displays an astronaut profile, mission information, and important health indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and respiratory rate.
Our project uses simulated health readings to demonstrate how astronauts' vital signs can be organized and monitored through a single dashboard. It provides a clear visual overview of health information through a futuristic and user-friendly interface.
AstroCare aims to demonstrate the importance of continuous health awareness during space missions, where astronauts face challenging environments and access to immediate medical assistance may be limited. Our goal is to explore how digital technology can support astronaut health monitoring and contribute to safer future space exploration.
details:
AstroCare is a responsive website with Home, Dashboard, and Monitoring sections. It displays astronaut mission details and four key health indicators: heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, and respiratory rate using simulated readings.

AstroCare organizes important health information in one dashboard, making it easier to view and understand. It aims to contribute to safer space exploration by demonstrating how digital technology can support astronaut health monitoring.

The website was developed using HTML and CSS in Visual Studio Code (VS Code), tested through a web browser, and deployed using Netlify. A laptop was used for development, and simulated astronaut health readings were used for demonstration.

AstroCare is a single-page website without a backend or database. During development, we learned the basics of web development, responsive design, dashboard creation, and deployment. We also understood that future versions could include real-time sensor data, NASA research datasets, and intelligent health analysis to support more advanced astronaut healthcare monitoring.
